patch.value: Propagate the docstring gate entry guard fix

The isMainInvocation entry guard swallowed realpathSync ENOENT and returned false, causing npm run docstring to exit 0 having scanned nothing — a mandatory release gate reporting success without doing its job. Propagate the throw instead so a broken environment fails loudly.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Defect: isMainInvocation caught realpathSync ENOENT on argv[1] and returned false, so the top-level selector called the no-op placeholder instead of main. npm run docstring exited 0 having scanned nothing — a mandatory release check reporting success without doing its job.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Fix: removed the try/catch around realpathSync(entry) so it propagates. Adopted the canonical reference implementation (pathToFileURL(realpathSync(entry)).href === moduleUrl) from pm-context, replacing the local self-resolution variant. An unresolvable argv[1] means the environment is broken after Node already loaded this file, and a broken environment must not silently satisfy a gate.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Verification: npm test passes (72 tests), npm run docstring exits 0 (3 files, 44 declarations), npm run coverage meets thresholds, and node --experimental-strip-types confirms isMainInvocation throws ENOENT on an unresolvable argv[1] instead of returning false.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Greptile (P2 on pm-beads) and CodeRabbit (Major on pm-slack) independently flagged the one-sided comparison in isMainInvocation: pathToFileURL(realpathSync(entry)).href === moduleUrl resolves only argv[1], leaving moduleUrl holding the symlink under --preserve-symlinks. Canonicalising both sides through realpathSync fixes it. Verified by measurement: with moduleUrl holding the symlink path, both-sides (new) returns true while one-sided (old) returns false.
